anya: Quick heads-up — bringing a new 65B quant variant into long-context CI. Focus: RoPE scaling + cache wrap correctness. Starting smoke runs now, tagging eng-ml for visibility.

devon: Run command I kicked off:
```
./runner --model redwood-65b-int8f4 --seq-lens 8192,32768 --kv-cache-mode=partial --batch-size 2 --trace kv,rope
```

devon: Early logs show a small class of failures when a long prefix crosses the 8k boundary and continues into a follow-up request. snippet:
```
[INFO] kv_cache: append at pos=8190 len=40 -> wrap at 8192, new_idx=38
[WARN] kv_lookup: mismatch at key_idx=0 expected_ts=1782103310 got=1782103309
[ERROR] rope: pos_scaling out_of_range for token_pos=8194 alpha=1.0002
```

marta: Is this only with int8f4 quant or seen on fp16 too?

devon: Repro on fp16 is rare. Failure rate ~0.5% on fp16, ~4.2% on int8f4 during the packed cross-boundary scenario. Quant seems to amplify numerical edgecases.

luke: Two quick hypotheses: (1) KV position offset isn't being reset/updated when we slice sequences across requests, so RoPE gets wrong pos indices; (2) quant noise nudges the boundary index rounding. We should log the `kv_pos_offset` and `rope_index` per request.

quant-bot: auto-check: eval-suite/longprefix-handoff shows a +2.1% perplexity delta on int8f4 vs fp16 for samples crossing chunk boundaries. Attn pattern degradation concentrated in later tokens.

anya: Can someone add instrumentation to the runner to emit kv offsets and the derived rotary scale? small JSON per request is fine. e.g. `{"req_id": ..., "kv_offset": 8190, "rope_scale": 1.0002}`

marta: As an immediate mitigation, we could force a cache flush when incoming request token_count + kv_offset > kv_window - margin. It's heavier but safe for canary traffic. Thoughts?

sre-bot: FYI the smoke job triggered a brief canary throttle at 1782103368 because latency jumped >2x for a subset of workers. Linked ticket: #INF-1234.

luke: Implementing a safe patch: on sequence boundary crossing, zero the local `kv_pos_offset` for that request and recompute rope indices from absolute token count. Pseudo:
```
if (kv_offset + req_len > kv_window) {
  // flush local window pointers
  kv_pos_offset = 0;
  recompute_rope_indices(abs_token_index_base);
}
```
This avoids relying on previous partial offsets.

devon: I'll run three variants in parallel: baseline, flush-on-boundary, rope-rescale-fix. Will collect perp & token-latency histograms. PR up in ~45m, pinging @luke for quick review.

quant-bot: Reminder: when measuring quality, include BLEU/ROUGE for regen tests and also token-level entropy to spot drift.

anya: Good plan. Please add a note in the PR about expected perf cost of flush (rough estimate: +7-12% token latency for affected requests). If flush fixes correctness, we can iterate on a cheaper selective-fix after root cause confirmed.

devon: Test run statuses: baseline=running, flush=queued, rope-fix=running. Will post results here when done.

anya: Thanks — keeping thread as single source for results. If anyone sees new failure modes please drop logs here. :rocket:
